chunks: And with this chain of transmission, he said:
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “The sorcerer of the Muslims is killed, but the sorcerer of the disbelievers is not killed.”
It was said: “O Messenger of Allah, and why is the sorcerer of the disbelievers not killed?” He said: “Because disbelief is greater than sorcery, and because sorcery and shirk are conjoined.”

key_terms.سَاحِرُ: a practitioner of sorcery or magic
key_terms.مَقْرُونَانِ: joined together; associated with one another
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: is to be killed; receives capital punishment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the ruling on a Muslim sorcerer and the relation between sorcery, kufr, and shirk?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling concerning sorcery and distinguishes between the Muslim practitioner of sorcery and the disbelieving practitioner. It also frames sorcery in theological terms by linking it with shirk and describing kufr as more grave.
